section_summary: The section begins with statistical appendices on Japanese fertilizers, chemical plants, coal, oil, and electric power. It then records U.S. and Far Eastern Commission proposals for removing industrial capacity as reparations while retaining facilities needed for civilian production. The final report on assured production capacity levels continues beyond page 198.

people.name: John H. Hilldring
people.role: State Department member of the State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee

people.name: Nelson T. Johnson
people.role: Secretary General of the Far Eastern Commission

people.name: Edwin W. Pauley

subfiles.title: Appendix III-A: Nitrogen fertilizer tables and synthetic ammonia plants
subfiles.about: Tabulates Japanese fertilizer trade, production and needs, and synthetic ammonia plant capacities.
subfiles.summary: Tables compare annual fertilizer imports, exports, production and consumption; estimate 1940–1945 production and needs; and list synthetic ammonia plants by location, company and nitrogen capacity.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-B: Sulphuric acid
subfiles.about: Gives 1929–1938 Japanese sulphuric acid production and estimated consumption by use.
subfiles.summary: Tables give production by concentration and consumption by ammonium sulphate, superphosphate, rayon and other uses.

subfiles.title: Appendix III-C: Calcium carbide and cyanamid
subfiles.about: Documents calcium carbide consumption, cyanamid inputs and Japanese plant capacity.
subfiles.summary: Tables trace 1929–1938 carbide production and use, estimate materials and electricity for carbide and cyanamid manufacture, and list cyanamid plants.

subfiles.title: Appendix IV: Japan's Coal Production and Resources
subfiles.about: Assesses coal available to Japan and supplies related coal and petroleum statistics.
subfiles.summary: The report argues that Karafuto was the only controlled territory that supplied a substantial share of Japan's coal, and recommends returning toward the pre-1931 balance between domestic production and consumption. It discusses Formosa, Korea and Manchuria, includes a coal chart and 1925–1944 coal table, and lists refinery capacity and synthetic and shale oil output.

subfiles.title: Appendix V: Report of Power Task Committee—Japan
subfiles.about: Evaluates Japanese electric generating capacity and regional grids for possible reparations removals.
subfiles.summary: The committee compares hydro and thermal capacity, generation and industrial demand across Japan's regional grids, drawing on OSS, Pauley, SCAP and Fullerton material. It generally recommends removing thermal plants and limiting hydro capacity to firm output, while qualifying those recommendations where local grids, coal mining or supply requirements warrant care. Extensive tables record grid use and capacity, including December 1945 figures.

subfiles.title: Proposed amendments to SWNCC 236/13: Assured Production Capacity Levels for Japan
subfiles.about: Submits amendments responding to SCAP objections and the draft Pauley reparations report.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring proposes dropping bearings and sulphuric acid from the assured list, reducing assured pig iron capacity to 500,000 tons, and raising chlorine capacity to 35,000 tons.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Commission letter transmitting interim reparations policy
subfiles.about: Transmits the Commission's unanimously approved policy for preparation of a directive to the Supreme Commander.
subfiles.summary: Johnson forwards the decision on steel, thermal power, soda ash, chlorine and caustic soda.

subfiles.title: Certification of Far Eastern Commission decision
subfiles.about: Certifies the attached text as adopted at the Commission's fifteenth meeting.
subfiles.summary: Johnson certifies the official text adopted on 12 June 1946.

subfiles.title: Interim Reparations Removals: Iron and Steel Industry; Thermal Electric Power; Soda Ash, Chlorine, and Caustic Soda Industry
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Sets capacity thresholds above which specified Japanese industrial facilities may be claimed.
subfiles.summary: The policy sets retention thresholds for steel ingot, pig iron, thermal power, chlorine, caustic soda and soda ash. It directs attention to regional power needs during removals.

subfiles.title: Memorandum forwarding draft directive on interim reparations removals
subfiles.about: Requests transmission of a draft directive implementing the Far Eastern Commission decision.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring asks that the directive go through the Joint Chiefs to General MacArthur.

subfiles.title: Directive regarding interim reparations removals
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: Recasts the Commission's steel, power and chemical capacity decision as operational instructions.
subfiles.summary: The draft instructs the Supreme Commander to make excess capacity available for claim, subject to safeguards for local electricity supply and possible review of the thermal power threshold.

subfiles.title: Statement of policy regarding interim reparations removals
subfiles.about: Restates the Commission's proposed thresholds for steel, thermal power and chemical facilities.
subfiles.summary: This enclosure reproduces the policy decision in recommendation form, including capacity limits and safeguards for electricity distribution.

subfiles.title: Comment on SWNCC 302, Reduction of Japanese War Potentials
subfiles.about: Questions the policy basis for using 1930–1934 living standards as Japan's reference level.
subfiles.summary: Rudlin argues that a calculation baseline risks becoming a restoration goal without adequate policy justification.

subfiles.title: Proposal for SWNCC Action on Removal of Synthetic Oil and Synthetic Rubber Industries
subfiles.about: Forwards a proposal to remove synthetic rubber and most synthetic oil capacity.
subfiles.summary: Galbraith seeks early SWNCC action while preserving equipment needed for ammonia fertilizer production.

subfiles.title: Memorandum submitting synthetic oil and rubber proposal to SWNCC
subfiles.about: Submits the State Department proposal for eliminating Japanese synthetic rubber and most synthetic oil capacity.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring requests prompt review after military comment from the Joint Chiefs.

subfiles.title: Proposal on Synthetic Rubber and Synthetic Oil Industries
subfiles.about: Proposes impounding Japanese synthetic rubber and oil plants for reparations or destruction.
subfiles.summary: The proposal calls for removal of all synthetic rubber facilities and synthetic oil equipment, except machinery SCAP judges necessary for synthetic ammonia fertilizer production. Its appendices quote related SWNCC, British, Pauley and SCAP proposals. The discussion cites wartime origins, limited civilian need, high costs and military uses as grounds for removal.

subfiles.title: Approval and distribution of assured production capacity levels
subfiles.about: Reports SWNCC approval of the amended capacity paper and requests its distribution.
subfiles.summary: Hilldring asks that the U.S. Far Eastern Commission member receive the paper and present Appendix C.

subfiles.title: Decision amending SWNCC 236/19
subfiles.about: Directs replacement of two pages after approval of the amended report.
subfiles.summary: Holders are instructed to substitute revised pages 227–228.

subfiles.title: Assured Production Capacity Levels for Japan: Note by the Secretaries
subfiles.about: Circulates the revised report and notes referral to the Joint Chiefs of Staff.
subfiles.summary: The secretaries circulate SWNCC 236/19 for consideration and military comment.

subfiles.title: Assured Production Capacity Levels for Japan
subfiles.from: State-War-Navy Coordinating Subcommittee for the Far East
subfiles.about: Recommends minimum Japanese industrial capacity that could be designated for permanent retention.
subfiles.summary: The report proposes assured capacity levels to encourage civilian industrial recovery while leaving other facilities open to final reparations decisions. Its proposed policy covers machine tools, shipbuilding, steel, pig iron, thermal power and chemicals, while assigning no assured level to arsenals, aircraft or light metals. The annex explains the use of minimized civilian requirements and begins detailed calculations for machine tools, ships and steel. The report continues beyond page 198.
